title: Get a planning permit before starting a use or development that needs one
what: Get development approval (a permit) before carrying out development, or starting a use of land, that the planning scheme says needs one, and keep to the approval.

laws.title: Land Use Planning and Approvals Act 1993 (Tas)

sources.title: Land Use Planning and Approvals Act 1993 (Tas)
sources.quote: A person must not commence any use or development which, under the provisions of a planning scheme, requires a permit unless the planning authority which administers the scheme, the Commission, or the Tribunal, has granted a permit in respect of that use or development and the permit is in effect or a major project permit has been granted in respect of that use or development and the permit is in effect.

sources.title: Land Use Planning and Approvals Act 1993 (Tas)
sources.locator: s 3, words naming the body (found 18 Nov 2026) (current)

reach.condition: if the planning scheme requires a permit for its use or development

confidence_note: The Act's own words bar starting a use or development that needs a permit without one.

assessment.summary: Zoning and planning approvals limit how many homes can be built and where businesses can open. They push house prices far above the cost of building, add delays and paperwork, and can shelter existing businesses from new rivals. The Productivity Commission puts the cost of housing regulation at about 1% of GDP a year, mostly from zoning.

marks.reason: Zoning keeps house prices well above the cost of supply: a large distortion in the largest asset market.
Zoning and approvals limit the sites open to new businesses; the Harper Review found planning rules can favour incumbents.
Development approvals add paperwork, holding costs and delay to building homes and business premises.

assessment.confidence_note: No city estimate of the zoning premium was found for this jurisdiction; the marks rest on the Productivity Commission's national estimate and the common design of planning systems. Marks copied from the register item tas-planning-zoning so the two agree.
